hints: Define one boolean per pair of prefixes: does the first `i` letters of the text match the first `j` characters of the pattern?
When the pattern's next character is an ordinary letter or a `.`, it must consume exactly one letter of text, so the answer comes from one cell diagonally back.
A `*` is the hard case, and it has exactly two readings: the thing before it appears zero times, or it appears once more.
Zero times means skipping two pattern characters. Once more means consuming one text letter and keeping the same pattern position - which is what lets it repeat.
